noticias.titular: Claude’s projects go from folder to conversation that splits the work into threads
noticias.entradilla: In September Anthropic announced a redesign of Claude’s projects, in beta and for Claude Code: users describe what they need and Claude divides it into tasks that run in the cloud.
noticias.imagen_alt: Diagram: on the left, a conversation called “Coordinator” splits the work into three threads, each with its own branch, inside a box labelled “In the cloud”; the threads return their results to a shared “Memory”. Labels: Coordinator, In the cloud, Threads, Memory.

noticias.titular: A train travel agency is used to practise basic maths in secondary school
noticias.entradilla: Felip Sarroca has used Claude Code to create a game-style activity for mixed-ability groups in secondary school (ESO) and shares the code and a guide for adapting it.
noticias.imagen_alt: A train follows a track; a ticket points to “Timetables and prices”. The track is closed (“Track closed”, marked with a red cross) and a blue detour, “Another route”, leads to the “Destination”. Labels: Timetables and prices, Another route, Track closed, Destination.

noticias.titular: Elemental Cómics presents the periodic table with a comic for each element, according to its author
noticias.entradilla: An interactive periodic table that, according to its author, opens each element as a comic followed by comprehension activities. It was created by Ernest Boixader and is shared under an open licence.
noticias.imagen_alt: A colourful periodic table on a dark background, with the title “Elemental Cómics”, filter buttons for the families and the first rows of elements.

noticias.titular: A Coursera report measures demand for AI and human-skills courses
noticias.entradilla: The Global Skills Report 2026, published in September, uses data from the Coursera and Udemy platforms and presents an index combining learning activity with each country’s readiness for AI.
noticias.imagen_alt: Two overlapping circles, “AI courses” and “Human skills”; the shared area is the “New index”. A globe accompanies the label “98 countries”. Labels: AI courses, Human skills, New index, 98 countries.

noticias.titular: HeyGen clones a voice for avatar videos, and its free plan allows three a month
noticias.entradilla: The tool turns a text into audio or into a video with a presenter, using a voice cloned from a short recording. Only an adult can use it, and only with the consent of the person whose voice it is.
noticias.imagen_alt: A microphone with a sound wave, labelled “Own voice”, leads by an arrow to a simply drawn presenter with sound waves coming from the mouth, labelled “Avatar”; on the right, a paper script, labelled “Script”, with an arrow towards the presenter; below, in red, “With consent”.

noticias.titular: DigComp 3.0 arrived and the teachers’ framework was expected; a year later it is still a draft
noticias.entradilla: In November 2025, the European Commission put AI into the digital competence framework for citizens, and teachers asked when theirs would follow. The final version is not expected until spring 2027.
noticias.imagen_alt: Diptych. On the left, “Nov. 2025”: the “DigComp” document with a tick and the “DigCompEdu” document with a question mark. On the right, “Today”: the first still has its tick and the second, “Draft”, is a document with a dashed border and a pencil.

noticias.titular: The conversation continued in Vibe Coding Educativo about whether it is better to program with AI agents…
noticias.entradilla: The conversation continued in Vibe Coding Educativo about whether it is better to program with AI agents from the console or from the desktop app. One view held that the power is the same and the difference lies in autonomy: tasks that run on their own, without anyone requesting them; another replied that you can also automate from the app, in the cloud or with a computer left on, although it was admitted that for more advanced use of agents the console seems the better option. It was covered in the article Console or app: teachers compare how to work with a programming agent.

noticias.titular: Vibe Coding Responsable 4.0: anything published openly must be reusable
noticias.entradilla: Version 4.0 of Juan José de Haro’s guide explains that the educational exception in copyright law does not cover what is published on an open website.
noticias.imagen_alt: Two shelves of images. On the left, a closed shelf with a padlock labelled “Closed classroom”. On the right, an open shelf with a verification badge labelled “Known licence”. Between them, an arrow labelled “Open”.

noticias.titular: OECD and EU set out four areas of AI literacy for primary and secondary schools
noticias.entradilla: The non-binding AILit framework describes in 19 competences, with three levels of progression and classroom examples, what students should know, do and value when it comes to artificial intelligence.
noticias.imagen_alt: Staircase of four ascending steps labelled “Engage”, “Create”, “Manage” and “Design”; above each step there is one dot per competence: seven on the first and four on each of the others. On the right, a card with three lines of increasing length and the label “3 levels”.

noticias.titular: Eight EU criteria for choosing and evaluating digital educational content in the classroom
noticias.entradilla: A non-binding European Commission guide supports teachers and school leadership teams from selecting a resource to evaluating its effect.
noticias.imagen_alt: An octagon with eight vertices and spokes from the centre, labelled “Eight criteria”. Inside, an irregular blue line joins points at varying distances from each vertex, marking a resource's strengths and weaknesses. A red magnifying glass points at one of the vertices, labelled “Legal compliance”.

noticias.titular: Transcribe audio and video and create subtitles without the file leaving your computer
noticias.entradilla: Transcribe turns recordings into text and subtitles with the Whisper model, inside the browser and without sending anything to third parties. It was created by Juan José de Haro.
noticias.imagen_alt: The Transcribe page with buttons to select audio or video and to import SRT or VTT files, the Whisper model selector, the transcription status and the box for the extracted text.

noticias.titular: Ideogram lets you repeat the same character across several images for classroom materials
noticias.entradilla: The image tool includes a free plan with weekly credits. On that plan, images are public, and students who are minors need their family’s permission.
noticias.imagen_alt: Three reference images of a character, labelled “References”, and an arrow pointing to four panels showing the same character in different scenes (sun, waves, tree and cloud), labelled “Same character”.

noticias.titular: Removing Gemini’s visible watermark was a paid perk; a year on, it takes one setting
noticias.entradilla: In November 2025 it was surprising that Google let some subscribers remove the mark that flags their images as AI-generated. Since August 2026, almost any user can switch it off; the invisible mark stays.
noticias.imagen_alt: Diptych of two identical images. On the left, “Nov. 2025”: an image with a visible star in the corner and a padlock, labelled “Ultra only”. On the right, “Today”: the same image with the star crossed out in blue and a switched-on toggle, labelled “One setting”.

noticias.titular: The ja.cat link shortener failed to load on the morning of Wednesday 25th and, according to a comment in…
noticias.entradilla: The ja.cat link shortener failed to load on the morning of Wednesday 25th and, according to a comment in the group, the cause was an incident at its DNS provider, Dinahosting. A temporary workaround was suggested in the group, but it only works on the computer where it is applied.

noticias.titular: Microsoft brings Elevate for Educators, AI training for teachers, to Spain
noticias.entradilla: The platform brings together courses, live seminars and a community of teachers, with three levels of recognition for teachers and another three for schools.
noticias.imagen_alt: Two staircases of three steps, one labelled “Teachers” and the other “Schools”, whose arrows lead to a group of people labelled “Teacher community”.

noticias.titular: Navarre plans to use AI in school inspection without saying which programs or what data
noticias.entradilla: The inspectorate’s action plan for the 2026-2027 school year includes AI as a support tool but does not specify tools or data safeguards, according to OKDIARIO.
noticias.imagen_alt: A document with a magnifying glass labelled “Inspection” points to a closed box with a question mark, labelled “AI as support” and “Unspecified”, and from it an arrow leads to a magnifying glass with a tick, labelled “Human review”.

noticias.titular: Connecting AI to Blender or Unreal uses up the usage limit very quickly, according to EduMedia-IAG
noticias.entradilla: According to the group, connecting coding assistants to 3D and video creation programs sends consumption soaring, although it works out cheaper than learning those programs.
noticias.imagen_alt: A terminal labelled “Agent” connects to a cube labelled “3D program” and to a film strip labelled “Video”, which lead to an almost empty battery labelled “Quota used up”; below, an open book labelled “Learning costs more”.

noticias.titular: Mis Gastos logs spending by category and charts it; it is used in History
noticias.entradilla: Luis Villanueva Aizcorbe created “Mis Gastos”, a Spanish-language web app for logging expenses by category and viewing daily, monthly and yearly totals. According to its author, he uses it in his History classes.
noticias.imagen_alt: The “Mis Gastos” app: a blue and green header with the motto “Controla tu dinero y vivirás mejor”, four totals at zero euros and the form with date, category, amount and description.

noticias.titular: Let’s keep virtual reality headsets for tasks where the point of view matters
noticias.entradilla: To draw a cove, a map may be enough. To work out at which bend in the path the lighthouse drops out of sight, it does make sense to step into the landscape.

noticias.titular: FLUX.2 only made images; a year on, its successor also generates video with sound
noticias.entradilla: In November 2025, Black Forest Labs launched FLUX.2, an image model that could be downloaded. In July 2026 it unveiled FLUX 3, which learns from images, video and audio at the same time.
noticias.imagen_alt: Diptych split by a vertical line. On the left, labelled “Nov. 2025”, an image icon labelled “Image”. On the right, labelled “Today”, the same image icon and, highlighted in blue, a video camera icon labelled “Video” and a speaker icon labelled “Sound”.

noticias.titular: A first trial of Project Genie, Google’s tool for creating interactive worlds, has been shared in…
noticias.entradilla: A first trial of Project Genie, Google’s tool for creating interactive worlds, has been shared in EduMedia-IAG: the controls took some getting used to. The paper has already published an article on Genie 4 in Project Genie.

noticias.titular: According to what was explained in the Vibe Coding Educativo group, the privacy guide that uses a traffic…
noticias.entradilla: According to what was explained in the Vibe Coding Educativo group, the privacy guide that uses a traffic light to classify the tools analysed by the INTEF (Spain’s National Institute of Educational Technologies and Teacher Training) no longer shows the apps from the group’s repository, because that information is now in the repository itself. Background: the guide, published as a website with search.

noticias.titular: Gemini now shows one user the option to switch off the use of their conversations to train Google’s…
noticias.entradilla: Gemini now shows one user the option to switch off the use of their conversations to train Google’s models, according to a screenshot shared in ChatGPT-IA-edu. Background: the announced change.

noticias.titular: According to the poster shared in ChatGPT-IA-edu, the INTEF is keeping enrolment open until 27 November…
noticias.entradilla: According to the poster shared in ChatGPT-IA-edu, the INTEF is keeping enrolment open until 27 November for the NOOC (a very short open online course) “IA en las aulas: normativa, riesgos y oportunidades” (AI in the classroom: regulation, risks and opportunities).

noticias.titular: The INTEF’s privacy guidelines move from a PDF to a website with search and filters
noticias.entradilla: The guide uses a traffic-light system to classify the 1,144 tools analysed by the INTEF.
noticias.imagen_alt: A traffic light with three lights: the red one, labelled “Do not use”; the amber one, labelled “With school permission”; and the green one, labelled “Can be used”. On the right, a list with a magnifying glass and the label “1,144 tools”.

noticias.titular: South Korea’s education minister resigns over measures against AI cheating
noticias.entradilla: Last-minute changes to prevent the use of AI in the national university entrance exam caused difficulties for students and teachers.
noticias.imagen_alt: Three steps from left to right: a pencil labelled “Pencil only”, a mobile phone crossed out with a red line and labelled “No phones”, and a person labelled “Resignation”.

noticias.titular: A comparison tool helps you choose which free chatbot suits your needs
noticias.entradilla: Juan José de Haro created a web app where you rate the importance of each feature and get a personalised ranking of free chatbots.
noticias.imagen_alt: Two columns: on the left, sliders for the importance of each feature; on the right, the ranking of chatbots with percentages, led by Qwen on 91%.

noticias.titular: Affinity brings photo editing, vector drawing and page layout together in one free program
noticias.entradilla: It is useful for retouching and composing images generated with AI. Its official website presents it as free for individuals, with the AI features available only on Canva’s paid plans.
noticias.imagen_alt: Loose, tilted images, labelled “Loose”, pass through three tools, a brush (“Photo”), a pen (“Vectors”) and a grid (“Layout”), which converge in a single window where a poster page remains, with a title, two images and a caption, labelled “Poster”.

noticias.titular: Opus 4.5 scored above 80% on a coding test that OpenAI no longer uses
noticias.entradilla: In November 2025, a record on a coding benchmark was celebrated as a sign that AI had no ceiling. Three months later, OpenAI stopped publishing results on it, calling it flawed and contaminated.
noticias.imagen_alt: Diptych split by a vertical line. On the left, “Nov. 2025”: a code file with a verification seal and the labels “SWE-bench” and “Record”. On the right, “Today”: the same file with a blue prohibition symbol and the label “Withdrawn”.

noticias.titular: Raül Torres has come off the waiting list for Project Genie, the Google model that creates interactive…
noticias.entradilla: Raül Torres has come off the waiting list for Project Genie, the Google model that creates interactive worlds, and has access through his Google AI Pro subscription, as the paper reported when presenting Genie 4.

noticias.titular: An imagined case asks who signs a prize-winning story illustrated with AI
noticias.entradilla: An instalment of the series “Familias con inteligencia” imagines a case: a student declares that they used AI, wins a competition and a classmate challenges it. Chema Falcó asks schools for clear criteria.
noticias.imagen_alt: Three labels, “Text”, “Creative direction” and “Execution”, grouped by a brace that points to a book labelled “Story”; below, a notice with a medal and the label “Competition rules”, with a dashed red arrow towards the story.

noticias.titular: An app turns spoken answers into assessment reports for families
noticias.entradilla: “Informes a viva voz”, by Ernesto Boixader, asks teachers to answer three or seven questions about each student, and AI writes the report from those answers.
noticias.imagen_alt: A microphone labelled “Voice”, with the label “3 or 7 questions”, an arrow to a robot labelled “AI writes” and another to a document labelled “Report”; below, a person with the label “Teacher reviews”.

noticias.titular: Raül Torres releases his short film “Buzz” and explains step by step how he made it
noticias.entradilla: The director explains on a web page and in a video how he shot it by hand in virtual reality and left only the developing of the images to AI.
noticias.imagen_alt: A chain of four steps with arrows: a cube labelled “3D set”, virtual reality glasses labelled “Shot by hand”, a robot labelled “AI develops” and a clapperboard labelled “Buzz”; beneath the two middle steps, a dashed red bracket.

noticias.titular: An editor that turns ABC notation into a score and plays it in the browser
noticias.entradilla: María Teresa González created a simple music editor: you type the melody as text, the score appears and you can listen to it, with nothing to install.
noticias.imagen_alt: Editor with a text box in ABC notation on the left and, on the right, the audio controls and the score of a C major scale.

noticias.titular: Google offered Opal for building apps without coding; a year later it has shut it down
noticias.entradilla: In November 2025, Google offered Opal for free, a tool for building apps with AI without knowing how to code. It shut it down on 17 November 2026, and what people made with it does not move to Gemini on its own.
noticias.imagen_alt: Diptych split by a vertical line. On the left, labelled “Nov. 2025”, an app window labelled “Opal”. On the right, labelled “Today”, the same window crossed out with a red cross and labelled “Closed”, and a blue arrow pointing to a forward-slash icon labelled “Skills”.

noticias.titular: AI helps learning more when it is used to understand than when it does the task
noticias.entradilla: A review by Stanford University now brings together 52 studies measuring the effect of AI on learning: using it to understand new material fares better than using it to produce the work, although no use improves results consistently. This report explains how to read those studies, why a tutor that asks questions is not enough on its own and what a teacher can do so that AI does not do the students’ work.
noticias.imagen_alt: Infographic: a student facing an AI assistant with two paths. At the top, “Hand in”: the AI does the work and, without the tool, the result falls: “Without the tool: −17%”. Below, “Understand”: the assistant asks questions and the student corrects their own errors: “64% self-corrected”. Underneath, four recommendations: “Try it first”, “Tutor asks”, “Split the tasks” and “Check without AI”.

noticias.titular: Gemini Notebook now has an official API, though limited and in preview
noticias.entradilla: It lets other programs create notebooks and add sources to them, but only with personal accounts. An unofficial code library does more, although it may stop working without warning.
noticias.imagen_alt: A diagram of two paths to the same notebook: the upper one, labelled “Official API”, passes through a padlock and carries the label “Personal only”; the lower one, labelled “Unofficial”, is a dashed red line with the label “May break”. On the right, the notebook, labelled “Notebook”.

noticias.titular: Android lets you share your own app with up to 50 devices without Google Play
noticias.entradilla: The limited distribution account is free and is intended for people who build apps for a class or a small group.
noticias.imagen_alt: A QR code, labelled “QR code”, with an arrow towards a grid of phones followed by an ellipsis and the label “Up to 50 devices”; below, a red cross and the label “No Google Play”.

noticias.titular: An Argentine handbook brings the environmental, labour and social costs of AI into the classroom
noticias.entradilla: Two researchers propose that secondary school teachers ask what for, from where and with what consequences artificial intelligence is used, before deciding how. The 2026 handbook takes a Latin American and feminist perspective.
noticias.imagen_alt: Layered diagram: a screen labelled “AI assistant” rests on three stacked layers, “Decisions”, “Data centres” and “Labelling”, while a magnifying glass descends through them beside a red arrow and the question “With what consequences?”.

noticias.titular: Since October, Gemini has offered visual, interactive tours of topics for studying
noticias.entradilla: Immersive explorations are a library of ready-made topics explored layer by layer. According to the group, you cannot create your own topics, and the experience is available in only six languages, not including Spanish.
noticias.imagen_alt: On the left, concentric circles like layers to be explored, labelled “In layers”; on the right, a globe crossed out with a red line, with the labels “6 languages” and “No Spanish”.

noticias.titular: A simulator lets you build Rube Goldberg machines and analyse their levers
noticias.entradilla: Students place pieces on a board, set the chain going and check the fulcrum, load and force of each simple machine. It is in Catalan.
noticias.imagen_alt: A lever on a triangular fulcrum, labelled “Fulcrum”; on the left, a red downward arrow labelled “Force”, and on the right, a block on the lever labelled “Load”.

noticias.titular: The image model that drew a nine-sided shape with eleven sides has been replaced in Gemini
noticias.entradilla: In November 2025, Google’s new image model got some polygons right and others wrong. In February 2026 Nano Banana 2 replaced it in Gemini, and for developers there is another that costs a quarter as much per 1K image.
noticias.imagen_alt: Diptych split by a vertical line. On the left, “Nov. 2025”: four ink-coloured banknotes and below them “$0.134”. On the right, “Today”: a single blue banknote, a quarter as many, and below it “$0.0336”.

noticias.titular: Google DeepMind offers, in English, an interactive guide that uses its Gemma 4 model to explain how a…
noticias.entradilla: Google DeepMind offers, in English, an interactive guide that uses its Gemma 4 model to explain how a language model, the kind of program behind ChatGPT, generates from a text the fragment that comes next. It goes through five stages, from splitting the text to the chat format.

noticias.titular: The Council of the EU approves conclusions on citizens’ AI skills
noticias.entradilla: Member states back the idea that people of all ages should learn to use artificial intelligence critically and responsibly. These are policy guidelines, not a rule that binds schools.
noticias.imagen_alt: A diagram of three steps joined by arrows: a building with columns, “European framework”; a flag, “Each state”; and an open book, “Classrooms”. The dotted red arrow between the last two is labelled “Guidance only”.

noticias.titular: Chicago weighs its options if Google withdraws search from districts that reject its AI
noticias.entradilla: According to the Chicago Sun-Times, Google warns that school districts that do not allow its AI tools will lose access to search next year.
noticias.imagen_alt: A building, “District”, with an arrow labelled “Rejects AI” pointing to a magnifying glass crossed out with a red circle, “Search”, and below it the question “No access?”.

noticias.titular: A Catalan-language train puzzle for planning shunting moves is new in the repository
noticias.entradilla: The Vibe Coding Educativo resource repository adds eight resources in the week ending 20 November: one is presented here and seven have already had their own article.
noticias.imagen_alt: Welcome screen of the game over a track layout with colourful numbered wagons, with a field for typing a player name.

noticias.titular: Manchester Animation Festival will not accept films made with generative AI from 2027
noticias.entradilla: The British festival announced it on 13 November together with this year’s awards. Its director presents it as a way of backing animation artists.
noticias.imagen_alt: A film clapperboard, “AI film”, with an arrow labelled “From 2027” cut by a red bar that does not reach the building with columns, “Festival”.

noticias.titular: Trama adds readings grouped into “universes” and versions of different difficulty
noticias.entradilla: The reading-comprehension catalogue lets you choose readings that share the same world and versions of the same text at different levels. Its author asks for help translating it into Galician, Basque and Aranese.
noticias.imagen_alt: On the left, three open books inside a dotted circle, “Universe”; on the right, three stacked sheets with lines of text of different lengths, “Variants”.

noticias.titular: From 9% to 36% in research-level physics: AI still fails almost two in three
noticias.entradilla: In November 2025 a new evaluation of unseen physics problems was launched, and no AI model reached 10%. A year later, the best result is close to 36%.
noticias.imagen_alt: Diptych in two halves. On the left, labelled “Nov. 2025”, a sheet with three physics challenges, all three crossed out, and the label “Fails almost everything”. On the right, labelled “Today”, the same sheet with the first challenge solved, with a blue mark, and the other two still crossed out, with the label “Still fails a lot”.

noticias.titular: Gemini will separate conversation history from permission to train models
noticias.entradilla: Google will replace the “Keep Activity” setting with two: one for history and, separately, one that lets its models use the content of conversations.
noticias.imagen_alt: A switch labelled “Keep Activity” splits, with two arrows, into two independent settings: “History”, with a calendar and a switch, and “Training”, with a cogwheel and another switch.
